text:
marta: Heads-up — saw a regression on the hotset hit-rate after yesterday's kernel selector change. GPU nodes started hitting OOM during 95th percentile tails.
liam: Which change specifically? the `kernel.auto_select` tweak?
marta: yes, we flipped fallback preference from `vect_fast` -> `kern_v2_opt` for <128 tokens. seems fine for latency but KV cache pressure rose.
anya: do we have heatmaps? can we see prefix distribution before/after?
perf-bot: perf-summary: hostgroup gpu-prod-7, 2026-03-17 03:11 -> hit-rate drop -11% on KV prefix cache; median p99 latency +8ms; memory pressure spikes on 3/6 hosts. Logs: `OOM: mem_alloc_failed` 12 events.
raj: quick idea: the new kernel reduces per-token compute time so throughput for short prefixes increased — more concurrent in-flight contexts, larger active KV set, hence more items resident in GPU cache.
simon: also kernel change changed stride allocation pattern — we now allocate slightly larger KV slab for same key due to alignment diff. fragmentation increased.
liam: can we repro in staging? which config toggles to flip back?
marta: repro in staging with a ramp: patch the selector and run the canonical prefix workload (prefix-mix-v3). I have a reproducer script: ```bash
./bench_prefix.py --workload prefix-mix-v3 --qps 200 --duration 10m
```
anya: numbers from staging: before flip: gpu_cache_hitrate 0.84, after flip: 0.73. avg slab_frag 0.12 -> 0.27.
raj: two levers: reduce concurrent inflight (batcher.window_ms + max_inflight) OR tune cache eviction (ttl/softcap/reclaim).
ops-sre: production mitigation: set `kernel.auto_select=baseline` on hot nodes, rolling restart? deploy-bot: rollback patch 6783 queued, ETA 10m if approved.
marta: short-term mitigation: raising `kv_cache.soft_cap_fraction` to 0.65 and enabling `reclaim_fraction=0.2` looks promising in staging (recovered hit-rate to 0.80, less fragmentation).
liam: curious about TTL tradeoffs — raising TTL can keep hot prefixes resident but may increase fragmentation. what did you try?
marta: tried `kv_cache.ttl_ms` from 30000 -> 60000 for prefix buckets and `ttl_bucket_count` from 8->16 to spread eviction intervals. resulted in slightly higher memory use but hit-rate up +4%.
anya: propose a two-phase plan: 1) emergency rollback to baseline selector on affected fleets; 2) deploy softcap + reclaim + TTL bucket smoothing across canary; 3) iterate on batcher/window heuristics to cap inflight for short kernels.
simon: long-term: we should add kernel-aware cache sizing — i.e., per-kernel expected in-flight multiplier that adjusts `cache.max_bytes_gpu` dynamically.
raj: add a sampler to measure per-key allocation size delta across kernels (to catch stride/alignment regressions early).
marta: I'll open a short RFC with experiments and config matrix. For now I'll greenlight rollback.
liam: also add a small perf regression test: run prefix-mix-v3 under both kernels for 30m with slab fragmentation telemetry. we can gate selector flips on that.
ops-sre: leaving a note — increasing soft_cap_fraction may raise eviction latency spikes, watch p95/p99 eviction duration. set alert if eviction_time_ms > 200.
perf-bot: experiment results (staging): rollback -> p99 latency back to baseline; softcap+reclaim -> hit-rate stable at 0.79, fragmentation down 40% vs post-change.
marta: thanks. I'm going to kick the rollback and post an RFC link when ready. @liam @anya please triage the sampler + perf test. :thumbsup:
liam: on it, will add sampler PR and test harness.
anya: will draft RFC and include config knobs and canary rollout plan.
deploy-bot: rollback 6783 started on fleet gpu-prod-7 at 2390124715.
ops-sre: monitoring: 3 hosts recovered memory pressure after rollback, no further OOM events.
raj: follow-up todo: 1) add kernel-aware cache heuristics, 2) sampler + alarm, 3) perf gate for selector flips, 4) document softcap/reclaim knobs.
marta: leaving this open until next cadence; will update thread with RFC link and experiment IDs.
